text:
sara_sales: Heads-up — AcmeCorp POC demo just hit a spike of 5xx errors during the live run. ~20 parallel users, started at 15:02 UTC. They reported a mix of 503/504 and some 500s. Anyone on call? :grimacing:

alex_eng: I'm on it. Can you paste a few example request_ids and exact time window (start/end)? Any deploys in the last 10m?

sara_sales: window 2026-03-21T15:02:00Z - 15:06:00Z. sample ids: rq-01F2A3, rq-01F2A4, rq-01F2B0. No manual deploys from our side, customer was doing a scripted demo.

deploy-bot: autoscaler: scaled workers 2 -> 5 (policy: on-demand); triggered at 2026-03-21T15:03:12Z; warmup_est ~40s; cooldown 300s.

mike_sre: seeing `circuit_breaker` trips in the serving runtime around that time on the tenant route. Likely rate-shedding because backlog spiked and warmup lagged.

mike_sre: log snippet from runtime (/var/log/redwood/serve.log):
```
[15:03:15Z] route=acme-poc request_id=rq-01F2A3 queue_len=78 circuit_breaker=TRIPPED drop_pct=0.42 error=5xx
[15:03:16Z] model=redwood-large backend=gnmi-3 status=overloaded tokens_in_flight=124
```

paul_support: can you run the support bundle for that tenant and paste the link? Also run the queue-length metric over the window. Example command: `redwoodctl support bundle --tenant acme-corp --from 2026-03-21T15:00Z --to 2026-03-21T15:10Z`

alex_eng: explain what's happening: autoscaler did add workers but worker warmup (GPU context + kv cache) is ~35-45s. Meanwhile the circuit breaker is configured to start shedding when queue_len > 50 and error rate climbs. So during the warmup we saw a backlog >70 which tripped the CB and caused us to start returning 5xx quickly instead of waiting for workers to finish warmup.

jen_se: short-term mitigations for the demo: 1) failover the AcmeCorp route to `redwood-small` model (lower mem, faster startup), 2) temporarily raise the circuit-breaker threshold to 120, 3) enable prefix caching for repeated prompts. I can push the routing fallback now if you want.

sara_sales: please do fallback to smaller model — customer is fine with slightly lower quality for the demo, want it stable.

alex_eng: I'm going to flip a canary: route policy change to try `redwood-small` on 30% of traffic immediately, and bump CB threshold to 120. Will monitor.

deploy-bot: route:acme-poc updated by alex_eng at 2026-03-21T15:04:10Z (policy: fallback=redwood-small, fallback-traffic=30%)

mike_sre: also toggled `allow-warm-pool` for that pool so we keep at least 2 prewarmed workers; that should reduce warmup spikes.

paul_support: bundle uploaded: https://s3.redwood-internal/support-bundles/acme-2845012345.tgz — contains serve.log, worker-metrics, profiling. I'll attach to the case and flag for postmortem.

jen_se: quick config snippet for fallback (for notes):
```yaml
routing:
  tenant: acme-corp
  policy:
    primary: redwood-large
    fallback: redwood-small
    fallback_percentage: 30
```

alex_eng: initial results: error rate dropped to near 0% after fallback and warm-pool change. Visible latency improved from 1.2s median to 400ms. Still monitoring for any residual 5xx.

sara_sales: great, customer back on demo and reporting no more errors. thanks team.

mike_sre: postmortem TODOs: - analyze why warm-pool config didn't prevent this (should have been 2 prewarmed workers) - consider lowering autoscale step size so we don't overshoot queue pressure - evaluate increasing default CB threshold for POCs where warmup cost is high.

paul_support: action items: I uploaded logs, creating case RN-4721 and looping in enterprise sales for reserved capacity pricing.

jen_se: I'll draft an ops-safe runbook for POCs: recommended prewarm count, fallback rules, and demo checklist (prewarm before customer demo).

alex_eng: follow-up: I temporarily disabled aggressive rate-shedding for acme-corp and set `cb_threshold=120` for the route. Reverting to defaults after postmortem.

sara_sales: looping in customer success to schedule a follow-up and confirm demo replay. cc @paul_support @jen_se

paul_support: noted. Closing thread once postmortem items created and RN-4721 has next steps. :white_check_mark:

sara_sales: thanks all :pray:
